stories.label: Netanyahu's Likud, Eisenkot's Yashar end coalition talks without deal
stories.summary: Unity-government talks between caretaker PM Netanyahu's Likud and Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar collapsed after four hours, split on who leads and whether far-right minister Itamar Ben-Gvir stays in government. Lead with the Ben-Gvir question: the man who runs the police and the prison system holding Palestinians is the sticking point. The mechanism: without a deal Israel stays under a caretaker government, which decides Gaza and the West Bank with no new mandate.

stories.label: Democrats secure largest House majority in election in three decades
stories.summary: Decision Desk HQ projects Democrats at 258 House seats, the largest majority won in a regular election in three decades, including districts they had long lost, such as Virginia Foxx's in North Carolina. Lead with the number and what it hands the opposition for Trump's last two years: subpoenas, the power of the purse, and control of war-powers and impeachment votes. The surprise is where the seats came from.

stories.label: Yemen has been target of 5,581 Saudi air and missile atta
stories.summary: The Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree, quoted by Iran's state Mehr News Agency, puts Saudi air and missile attacks on Yemen since the escalation began at 5,581, naming Marib and Sanaa. Attribute every figure, to Saree and to Mehr, and state none as fact. This is the side of the Saudi–Houthi exchange that gets little coverage: our recent stories covered Houthi missiles fired at Riyadh. Frame it around what the strikes do to Yemenis who are already living through famine.

stories.label: Durban port crisis and debt hurdles test SA's private rail overhaul
stories.summary: South Africa is betting its freight revival on opening Transnet's debt-laden rail network to private operators, while delays at the Durban Gateway Terminal, the country's main container port, keep backing up the export chain. Lead with the mechanism: miners and farmers pay when ore and citrus cannot reach the coast. Ask whether the public-private model can fix a monopoly that is short of capital.

stories.label: Crumbling services drive businesses from Ekurhuleni hub, putting R2.5bn at risk
stories.summary: Manufacturers in Wadeville, Ekurhuleni's industrial heart, say years of failing power, water and roads have cost an estimated R2.5bn in lost or delayed investment, while parties bargain over the metro's next administration. Lead with the R2.5bn. The structural point is that municipal collapse, not national policy, is now deindustrialising South Africa's manufacturing belt.

stories.label: Gold rush in Dubai as sharp drop in price attracts savvy shoppers | The National
stories.summary: Gold's slide on Fed-hike bets has filled Dubai's Gold Souq, the world's biggest retail hub for physical gold, with buyers, many of them South Asian workers who save in jewellery rather than in banks. Name the series: gold. Lead with who is buying the dip and why: in the Gulf and South Asia gold is household savings, so a falling price works as a transfer to them. Unlike the Karachi shortage story, this one is about demand.

stories.label: 开户热、缴费冷：个人养老金产品缺一套靠谱的独立第三方标尺
stories.summary: Chinese savers opened personal pension accounts in large numbers but put little money into them ('hot to open, cold to pay in'). TMTPost argues the scheme lacks an independent third-party rating of its products. The stakes: Beijing needs household savings to fund an ageing population, and the gap between accounts and contributions shows how little trust savers have in what they are sold. This is the Chinese financial press's own diagnosis.

stories.label: 刚刚，Claude黎曼猜想证明通过验证！菲尔兹奖得主回应“数学研究不存在了？”
stories.summary: The material development since our 2026-11-20 story: Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative issued a joint statement that Levent Alpöge's roughly 17-million-line Lean proof of the generalized Riemann hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions compiles, states the right theorem, and passes several independent proof checkers. MIT's Andrew Sutherland ran the checks with Claude Code. Lead with the inversion: the machine verified the proof before any human read it (the prose version runs to 250,000 pages), and a 940-page all-human candidate proof was found flawed by AI within hours. Fields medallist Ngô Bảo Châu accepts the result. The caveat: machine verification is not peer review, and the Clay prize process takes at least two years. Anthropic is Alpöge's employer: say so. Alpöge is trending on Wikipedia.

stories.label: Toyota, Nissan, and Honda to standardize parts to lower costs
stories.summary: Japan's three biggest carmakers, normally rivals, will standardise components to cut costs. Lead with why rivals are pooling now: Chinese EV makers such as BYD undercut them on price with vertically integrated supply chains. The mechanism is shared parts, which bring scale without a merger. Tech readers will see the parallel to an open standard, and the story drew 1,100+ points on Hacker News.

stories.label: Silver briefly forms a rare crystal structure seen in radioactive polonium
stories.summary: Hokkaido University researchers report in Nano Letters that silver can briefly take on the simple-cubic arrangement otherwise known only in polonium, and that in this form it is unusually reactive. Lead with the diamond-versus-graphite idea: the same atoms in a different arrangement give a different material. A metastable silver phase could matter for catalysts.

stories.label: Egypt uncovers sprawling ancient necropolis filled with coffins, gold artifacts
stories.summary: An Egyptian-led excavation at Tarrana in Menoufia province, in the Nile Delta, found a cemetery with hundreds of coffins and gold artefacts. Lead with the scale. Then the point: Egyptian teams, not foreign missions, now lead such digs, and the Delta's wet soil seldom preserves this much. Note how Cairo uses these finds to promote tourism.

stories.label: Russian ship likely hit in drone attack at Benghazi port
stories.summary: A Russian corvette, the Merkury, exploded at dawn at the Benghazi naval base, where it had stopped for fuel and supplies on its way home, and Libya's eastern government suspects a drone. Lead with where it happened: Benghazi is the Haftar-held port that anchors Russia's military presence in Africa, so the war on Russian shipping now reaches the Mediterranean, the same weekend a Russian-linked cargo ship burned in the Gulf of Finland. Say plainly who has and has not claimed it.

stories.label: Sanctioned Russian vessel ablaze in Finnish waters after drone attack
stories.summary: Follow-up to the 11-21 drone strike on a cargo ship out of Kaliningrad, with two new facts: the sanctioned ship, linked to Russia's Ministry of Defence, is still burning in Finnish waters and may sink, and Finland's prime minister now attributes the attack to Ukraine, saying the war is 'spilling over into our immediate vicinity'. Lead with the attribution: a NATO member publicly naming Kyiv for a strike in its own waters. Then the cost Finland carries, a possible wreck and spill in the shallow Gulf of Finland.

stories.label: Drone attacks kill five children, injures 10 in Khartoum and Omdurman
stories.summary: Dawn drone strikes across Khartoum and Omdurman killed five children, injured at least 10 people, and damaged homes and a UN building, according to eyewitnesses who spoke to Radio Dabanga. Lead with the children, and give the dead the same weight as any other conflict's. Then the mechanism: the capital, retaken and being repopulated, is still within drone range, so returning families are not safe. Name who the attacks are attributed to only as far as the source does.

stories.label: Zelenskyy urges US to release Patriot missiles as Russia kills 3 in Ukraine
stories.summary: A Russian drone attack killed at least two people near Kyiv, in Vyshhorod district, and shelling killed one in Zaporizhzhia, after a week of strikes on 20 regions. Zelenskyy is asking Washington to approve Patriot interceptors that are already paid for or promised. Lead with the dead, then the mechanism: Ukraine's air defence depends on a US export decision, at a time when the Pentagon is restricting defence ties with allies.

stories.label: Iran unveils dual-missile launcher, new 'missile city': What to know
stories.summary: Iranian commanders, among them Ahmad Vahidi, toured a new underground 'missile city' and showed a dual-missile launcher, telling Washington that the US-Israeli strikes did not destroy Iran's arsenal. Lead with the timing: the display comes during the Hormuz blockade standoff and the talks in Qatar, and it is a signal aimed at the negotiating table. Separate what was shown from what can be verified.

stories.label: Oman to supply petroleum products, $200m credit facility to PSO under new agreement
stories.summary: Pakistan State Oil signed a deal with Oman's state-owned OQ Trading for petroleum products plus a $200m credit line. Lead with the mechanism: Oman's ports sit outside the Strait of Hormuz, so Pakistan is paying to route its fuel around the blockade, and the credit line is what makes that affordable for a country short of dollars. Name the series: Brent crude and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.label: Residents lament another increase in cooking gas prices
stories.summary: Cooking gas in Abuja now sells for N1,600 to N2,000 per kg after another increase, and households tell NAN they are going back to charcoal and firewood. Lead with that reversal, which has costs for health and for forests, and then the mechanism: Nigeria exports gas while its own households pay import-parity prices, which rise when global energy prices move during the Hormuz crisis. Name the series: the naira, and natural gas.

stories.label: Glitch delays Delta flights in Atlanta as Thanksgiving travel spikes
stories.summary: A failure in the automation system that calculates weight and balance for departing flights caused a ground stop and hundreds of delays at Atlanta's Hartsfield-Jackson, Delta's hub and the world's busiest airport, on the weekend Thanksgiving travel begins. Lead with the single point of failure: a load-sheet system no plane can leave without. Connect it to the recent run of US outages, with numbers only from the sources.

stories.label: 87% of the Anthropic power will come from gas and 11% from coal in 2028
stories.summary: A breakdown of where AI data centres get their electricity: 'bring your own power' gas plants on site versus the grid. It projects that 87% of Anthropic's power in 2028 will come from gas and 11% from coal, and it drew 551 points and 623 comments on Hacker News. Lead with the figure, then the mechanism: grid connection queues push labs to build gas turbines behind the meter, which locks in fossil generation for decades as COP31 deadlocks over fossil-fuel finance. Treat it as an analysis and state its method and assumptions; it is not a company disclosure.

stories.label: Bitcoin's quantum threat goes beyond code to custodians, bridges, and 6 million coins
stories.summary: About 6 million bitcoin sit in addresses whose public keys are exposed, and moving them to quantum-resistant signatures requires every exchange, custodian and bridge to upgrade as well, not just the protocol. Lead with the governance deadlock: developers are split between freezing coins that never migrate (including lost and Satoshi-era coins) and keeping the upgrade voluntary, and neither has been adopted. The reader should come away understanding that this is a coordination problem, not a cryptography problem. Name the series: bitcoin.

stories.label: Atmospheric organic nitrogen emerges as a major nutrient source for global oceans
stories.summary: A study co-led by HKUST quantifies organic nitrogen that falls from the atmosphere onto the oceans, a part of the global nitrogen cycle that had been left out. Lead with the size of that input compared with the inorganic nitrogen that models already count, and with what it changes: how much plankton growth, and carbon uptake, is fed by pollution and dust blown off the land. Cite the journal and the numbers from the source.

stories.label: Israel's Eisenkot condemns arson attacks by Jewish settlers in West Bank
stories.summary: Settlers set fire to Palestinian cars and property in four villages including Deir al-Sudan and Deir Abu Mash'al, and DW reports an elderly Palestinian woman was killed by settlers. Lead with the victims and the villages, then the accountability gap: Israel has 'opened an investigation', but Eisenkot himself calls it 'Jewish terrorism' fuelled by ministers Smotrich and Ben Gvir, the men who run settlement policy and the police. Mechanism: the ministers responsible for law enforcement in the West Bank are the ones accused of enabling the attacks, so investigations rarely produce charges.

stories.label: Israeli fire kills four more in Gaza
stories.summary: Israeli strikes killed at least two Palestinians in the al-Mawasi area of Khan Younis, the zone Israel itself designated 'safe', and four in all on Sunday, more than a year into the US-backed ceasefire; the Gaza health ministry's toll now stands at 74,742. Displaced Palestinians protested. Lead with the deaths in al-Mawasi, then the mechanism: a ceasefire with no enforcement lets the killing continue a few at a time, below the threshold that draws attention. Follows our 2026-11-21 report on the winter floods in the tent camps.

stories.label: What's behind Iran's escalation of attacks in the Gulf?
stories.summary: New on Sunday: Iran hit a civilian economic site in Bahrain, and Saudi Arabia, Qatar and the UAE all condemned it. Qatar, the mediator in the US-Iran talks, rejected 'attacks on economic facilities, civilian objects and civilians'. The mechanism: the US naval blockade and sanctions are choking Iran's oil income, so Tehran is raising the cost for the Gulf states that host US forces and for the oil that leaves them, while a second US carrier, the Theodore Roosevelt, arrives to relieve the George Washington. Name Brent crude and ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz. Do not re-report the 11-21 Bahrain radar strike or the Khasab tankers except as context.

stories.label: Lithuania denies involvement in reported drone attack on Russia's Kaliningrad
stories.summary: New since our 11-21 report on the Gulf of Finland drones: a rare air alert sounded in Kaliningrad, and claims circulated of drone activity near the Baltic Fleet base at Baltiysk, reportedly the first attack on the exclave since the war began. Lithuania, whose territory any drone would cross, denied involvement. The mechanism: Kaliningrad is Russian territory wedged between two NATO states, so whoever launched the drones, the strike drags the alliance's frontier into the war. Report the claims as claims.

stories.label: Balen Shah's India Visit Is An Opportunity To Recalibrate Ties With Nepal
stories.summary: Balen Shah, the former Kathmandu mayor who became prime minister in March after the Gen Z uprising, makes his first official visit to New Delhi on Sunday at Modi's invitation. Lead with what a small, landlocked country that depends on India for fuel and transit wants, and what it can bargain with: hydropower exports, a border dispute over Kalapani and Lipulekh, and the room it has to lean toward China. Treat Nepal as the actor, not India's backyard.

stories.label: PTI MNAs demand to know whereabouts of party leaders detained in KP, seek their court production
stories.summary: PTI lawmakers from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa say party leaders and workers detained in the province have been held without disclosure of where they are, without being brought before a court, and without access to lawyers, against the backdrop of talk of governor's rule in KP. Lead with detainees whose families do not know where they are. The mechanism: holding people without producing them in court within 24 hours, as Pakistan's constitution requires, turns arrest into enforced disappearance and keeps courts out of the process.

stories.label: Young child dies in Virginia's first measles death of 2026
stories.summary: A child younger than four has died of measles in Virginia, the state's first measles death of the year. The state has not said whether the child was vaccinated. Lead with the child, then the mechanism: measles needs about 95% of people vaccinated to stop spreading, and US kindergarten coverage has fallen below that while federal health leadership has cast doubt on vaccines. A disease declared eliminated in the US in 2000 now kills children again.

stories.label: 方向盘收起的 10 秒，比亚迪在给下一个十年立标杆
stories.summary: BYD has shown a steering wheel that folds away in 10 seconds when the car drives itself, a claim to set the standard for what a self-driving cabin looks like. Lead with the hardware, and give the mainland view: the race in China is now over who defines the self-driving car, and the article argues that is scarcer than the technology. Mechanism: removing the wheel is a legal bet as much as an engineering one, because it presumes regulators will accept a car that no person can steer. If the source is commentary with no concrete product, the writer should drop it.

stories.label: 易天股份拟控股艾晨数能，主业承压下新管理层加码储能
stories.summary: Shenzhen display-equipment maker Etian (易天股份) plans to take control of Aichen Shuneng (艾晨数能) and move into power-supply and energy-storage gear for data centres, as its main business shrinks under new management. Lead with the pivot as a sign of where Chinese industrial capital is going: AI data centres are limited by power, so equipment makers are rebuilding themselves as suppliers of storage and power systems. Give the deal size and terms from the source.

stories.label: GLP-1 drugs could have a surprisingly large environmental payoff
stories.summary: New research estimates that wide use of GLP-1 appetite drugs such as Ozempic and Wegovy could cut food demand enough to free farmland larger than Italy. Lead with that figure. The mechanism: farm land use scales with calories eaten, so a drug that lowers how much people eat shrinks the land and emissions behind the food system. Also say who would gain, given that the drugs are priced for rich countries, and what happens to farmers, including grain exporters in the Global South.

stories.label: 中国异构计算何以“顶天立地”？
stories.summary: A Chinese-built 100,000-accelerator AI supercluster, Sugon's Shuguang 8000 in Zhengzhou, powered this year's ACM Gordon Bell Prize winner at SC26: an AI wavefunction calculation of nitrogenase's iron-molybdenum cofactor (113 electrons, 76 orbitals), with a 1.5km global weather model also a climate-prize finalist. Lead with the sanctions angle: all-domestic hardware, under US export controls, taking HPC's top application prize, scaling to 45,000 cards at 94.9% efficiency. The source is an industry-friendly mainland outlet; attribute the performance figures to it.

stories.label: 跨境收款之后，中国公司盯上智能体支付的新生意
stories.summary: Chinese cross-border payment firms are moving into 'agent payments', where AI agents pay on a business's behalf. The model shifts from charging channel fees to embedding operations inside companies' daily workflows. Lead with the mechanism: who holds the money and the liability when software, not a person, authorises a payment, and how Chinese firms are trying to set that standard before Western card networks do.

stories.label: 大众花巨资买软件，想拿回什么？
stories.summary: After three straight years of losses at its software unit CARIAD, Volkswagen has changed how it develops software and is buying it in at great expense, including from Chinese partners. Lead with the reversal: Europe's biggest carmaker is paying to import the software stack it failed to build, and China's EV makers now set the pace in the car's most valuable layer.

stories.label: Indonesia factory fire kills three, 36 missing
stories.summary: A fire destroyed the three-storey Fonusa Agung Mulia sweets factory in Serang, Banten, near Jakarta. At least three workers are dead and 36 missing; SCMP reports seven body bags recovered and up to 50 sought. Lead with the workers and the toll, then the accountability question: exits, fire licensing and inspection at Banten's dense industrial belt, and who answers for it.

stories.label: 'Population up in 40 China-border villages': Amit Shah reaches out to Arunachal amid dam protests
stories.summary: Delhi is courting Arunachal Pradesh while indigenous communities protest a mega-dam on the Siang. Amit Shah cites population growth in 40 China-border villages, and Kiren Rijiju calls for a 'balance' between tribal rights and investment. Lead with who bears the cost: Adi villages facing submergence for a dam Delhi frames as a strategic answer to China's Yarlung Tsangpo project upstream, so national security is being used to override land rights.

stories.label: Opposition questions US policy after report flags China's support to Pakistan during Op Sindoor
stories.summary: The US-China Economic and Security Review Commission's annual report says Chinese military support for Pakistan during the May 2025 India-Pakistan conflict complicated India's operations, and India's opposition is now questioning Washington's policy. Lead with what the commission documents about China's role (an independent US body, not government policy) and why it matters: the first major conflict where Chinese weapons and support were tested against a Western-armed military. Give Pakistan's position too; no Pakistani outlet is in the feed.

stories.label: Ukraine delivers massive strike on DPR's energy infrastructure overnight
stories.summary: State media only: Russian state news agency TASS reports that an overnight Ukrainian strike on energy facilities cut power to a large part of Russian-occupied Donetsk, quoting the occupation 'prime minister' Andrey Chertkov. Attribute every claim to TASS and the Russian-installed authorities. Frame it as the mirror image of Russia's long campaign against Ukraine's grid: civilians on both sides of the line now go into winter without power.

stories.label: Investors drive gold market as prices fall in Karachi
stories.summary: Gold's worst week in years has turned into a buying rush in Karachi. Heavy investor demand has emptied dealers of gold bars, which now carry premiums of Rs10,000-30,000 per tola, while wedding shoppers come back from silver and imitation jewellery. Lead with the bar shortage: Pakistanis treat gold as the savings account they trust over the rupee and the banks. Name the series: the gold price.

stories.label: Hormuz standoff puts Jordan in investment spotlight but transformation remains gradual | The National
stories.summary: The economic war in the Strait of Hormuz has pushed European governments to look for trade and energy routes that avoid the Gulf, and Jordan is being courted as a land bridge and electricity partner. Lead with the mechanism: a war 1,000km away is redrawing which Arab states Europe invests in. Then the catch: an IMF programme, debt and slow reform mean the change in Jordan is gradual. Name the series: ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.

stories.label: UK maritime agency reports second attack today on tanker in Hormuz
stories.summary: New development: two separate tanker attacks in one day off Oman's Khasab, on the outbound lane of the Strait of Hormuz, with Iran saying one vessel struck a naval mine. A mine is a different threat from a missile: it stays in the water after a ceasefire and keeps insurers out. The same day Foreign Minister Araghchi said reopening the strait is 'irrelevant' until Iran's demands are met. Tie it to ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Brent crude, and to who pays: Gulf exporters and the Asian importers behind them.

stories.label: Italy's ex-police chief dies amid probe into mafia case cover-up; suicide suspected
stories.summary: Gianni De Gennaro, Italy's national police chief and later intelligence coordinator, was under investigation for obstructing a reopened probe into the 1992 murder of anti-mafia magistrate Paolo Borsellino when he apparently took his own life at 78. Lead with the accountability question: 34 years on, the state's own top officers are suspects in hiding who killed the judge, and the death may close a line of inquiry. Report the death with care, without method detail.

stories.label: Denmark calls for restrictions for Russians after alleged rapper assassination plot
stories.summary: New development after the 2026-11-20 expulsion: Denmark has sent EU members a note asking them to issue Russians limited-territory visas that do not allow travel across Schengen, citing the foiled plot to kill Ukrainian rapper Kyivstoner. Lead with the mechanism: one state's security case is being turned into a bloc-wide visa rule, and the cost falls on ordinary Russian travellers as well as agents.

stories.label: 'Horrific' arrests at Seattle airport fuels anger at 'beyond reform' ICE
stories.summary: Masked ICE agents pulled travellers off a crowded jet bridge at Seattle-Tacoma, wrestling at least one woman to the ground and delaying a Los Angeles flight, and Washington's governor and a union have denounced it. Lead with the new ground: enforcement has moved past the security line onto the boarding bridge, during Thanksgiving travel. Name who was detained if the sources do, and what the state can and cannot do to stop federal agents in its airport. Use Reuters for facts over the Post's framing.

stories.label: Azerbaijan president begins 3-day visit to Vietnam
stories.summary: Ilham Aliyev and Vietnam's Prime Minister Le Minh Hung agreed in Hanoi to widen oil and gas, investment and trade ties, and to link rail freight through the Trans-Caspian (Middle) Corridor. Lead with the why: with Hormuz shut, Caspian producers and Asian buyers are looking for routes and suppliers that avoid the Gulf. Name what was actually signed, not the courtesy language.

stories.label: On defence, Japan's Takaichi caught between a weak yen and Trump
stories.summary: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi plans to rein in Japan's next five-year defence budget because a weak yen makes imported US weapons dearer and tax cuts have narrowed the fiscal room, and conservatives in her own party are pushing back while Washington wants more. Lead with the mechanism: the yen's fall is a defence-policy constraint, since much of the budget buys American hardware priced in dollars. Name the yen as the series.

stories.label: Pentagon moves to restrict defence ties with Canada
stories.summary: Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has issued a classified memo restricting military cooperation with Canada, a NATO ally and NORAD partner, and the Pentagon says it is 'refocusing' the relationship on American priorities. Lead with what is actually restricted, and with the structural point: the US is applying pressure to its closest ally through defence ties that both countries' continental air defence depends on. Dateline Ottawa if the effect lands there.

stories.label: South Korea education minister Choi Kyo-jin resigns amid AI cheating scandal
stories.summary: South Korea's education minister resigned on Sunday after an AI-assisted cheating scandal that began when the top scorer in a national tax accountant exam was found to have used AI, and spread to fears over the college entrance exam (suneung) last week. Lead with the precedent: the first cabinet minister to fall over AI cheating, in the country whose whole education system rests on one high-stakes exam. Explain how the cheating worked and what exam security is changing.

stories.label: 小鹏交出一份增长财报，盈利拐点为何还没来？
stories.summary: Xpeng posted record third-quarter revenue and deliveries yet still is not profitable. TMTPost asks why the profit turning point has not arrived, and whether overseas expansion and 'physical AI' (robotaxis, humanoid robots) can carry it. Lead with the gap between volume and margin in China's EV price war, from the mainland tech press's own reading, and give the figures.

stories.label: AI is being used to clone real people's videos
stories.summary: AI-generated characters on social media are copying real creators' videos frame by frame (their performances, their music, their scripts) and posting them as synthetic accounts that compete with the originals. Lead with a named creator whose work was cloned and with what the platforms do or fail to do when the copy is reported. The mechanism is that likeness and performance have no protection that the copiers have to respect.

stories.label: Tinubu campaigns in Ibadan, says Nigeria on path to prosperity
stories.summary: Nigeria's 2027 presidential race opened in Ibadan: Tinubu told the South-west that the sacrifices of his reforms (fuel-subsidy removal, the floated naira) will soon pay off, while Oyo governor Seyi Makinde's campaign, now a rival bid, mocked the rally's turnout and his four-year record, and the Wike-backed PDP disowned the opposition coalition and threatened to sue members who join it. Lead with the promise of prosperity against what the reforms cost households; the mechanism is an opposition split between a coalition and a PDP faction aligned with the president, which helps an incumbent. Dateline Ibadan.

stories.label: UK man swims in Strait of Hormuz to highlight environmental damage
stories.summary: The swim is the hook, not the story: Lewis Pugh, the UN Patron of the Oceans, swam in the Strait of Hormuz to document what months of attacks on oil tankers and gas carriers have spilled into one of the world's busiest waterways, and called for it to be reopened and cleaned up. Lead with the pollution nobody is counting and who lives off these waters (Omani and Iranian fishing communities); tie it to the collapse in ship traffic through the Strait of Hormuz under the blockade. Do not re-report the blockade itself, covered this cycle.

stories.label: BJP Accepts Public Mandate Following Loss In Rajasthan Local Elections
stories.summary: Congress won the Zila Parishad (district council) polls in Rajasthan, a state the BJP has governed since 2023, and the BJP state president conceded. Lead with the scale of the Congress win in the rural tier and why panchayat results matter: they are the widest test of rural anti-incumbency against a ruling party between state elections. Name the numbers the source gives; do not inflate a local result into a national verdict. Dateline Jaipur.

stories.label: Social norm strength varies between cultures with respect to norm referent, norm type, contextualization, normative properties, and valence - Communications Psychology
stories.summary: A cross-cultural study tests the leading theory that societies are simply 'tight' or 'loose' about norms, and finds instead that how strongly a norm binds depends on whose expectation it is, what kind of rule it is and the context. Lead with the most striking cross-country contrast the paper reports; the point for the reader is that a single tightness score for a whole culture, Muslim-majority ones included, hides more than it shows.
